author: Zuhayr Rahman Chowdhury
competitive_advantage: the world's strongest sports brand and athlete roster (including Jordan); rivals can't buy decades of brand heat.

statements.define: For athletes and sport-inspired consumers, especially young sneaker buyers, Nike offers performance and lifestyle footwear and apparel that help them perform and express identity.
statements.create: Nike wins on higher WTP: brand, athletes and innovation support premium prices (42.9% gross margin, FY2026). The brand is a sustained advantage; product innovation is now only temporary.
statements.capture: Rivalry and powerful retailers take value through discounting and shelf space. Nike's brand keeps pricing power, but its direct-to-consumer push ceded shelves to On and Hoka.
statements.deliver: Athlete marketing, innovation, outsourced manufacturing and rebuilt wholesale reinforce one brand-heat engine. Nike refuses owned factories and low-price lines; the risk is a slower innovation pipeline.

one_line: Nike sells brand heat at premium prices; watch whether innovation wins back share from On and Hoka.

define: **Who:** athletes and sport-inspired consumers, especially young sneaker buyers
**What:** performance and lifestyle footwear and apparel
**Problem solved:** perform better and express identity through sport
create: **WTP vs. cost:** wedge from WTP (brand, athletes); cost from outsourced scale
**Positioning map:** premium and on the frontier, pressured by On and Hoka
**VRI:** brand and Jordan sustained; innovation only temporary
capture: **Six forces:** rivalry and retailer (buyer) power are strongest
**Power:** brand pull beats most rivals; weaker with retailers after the direct-to-consumer push
deliver: **Activities:** athlete marketing, innovation, outsourced manufacturing, rebuilt wholesale
**Fit:** athletes create brand heat, full prices fund more athletes and innovation

who: Athletes and sport-inspired consumers worldwide, especially teens and young adults in sneaker culture
B2C: the consumer uses, decides and pays; retailers (Foot Locker, Dick's) are the channel
what: Hired to help them perform in sport and express identity through what they wear
Today they use Adidas, On, Hoka, New Balance, Asics or cheaper generic brands
problem: Generic shoes don't perform or signal status; niche brands lack range and cultural reach
Nike closes the gap with performance technology plus the strongest brand in sport
define.takeaway: Weakest premise: that young consumers still see Nike as the most exciting brand.

wtp_vs_cost: **Moves WTP:** brand and athletes, Jordan, Air and ZoomX innovation, cultural hype
**Table stakes:** comfort, fit, availability, everyday styling
**Cost levers:** outsourced manufacturing at scale, global sourcing, marketing scale
**Wedge:** higher WTP: premium prices with a 42.9% gross margin (FY2026)
map_reading: Axes: brand prestige and innovation vs price
Customers pick Nike for brand and sport; On and Hoka for running innovation
Nike, Adidas and Skechers sit on the frontier; New Balance sits inside it
create.takeaway: A WTP position resting on the brand more than on products.

vri.v: Yes: premium prices and demand pull
vri.r: Yes: no rival matches its reach
vri.i: Hard: decades of path-dependent brand building

vri.r: Partly: On and Hoka out-innovated it in running
vri.i: Imitable: rivals catch up within a product cycle

create.vri_takeaway: The brand holds; products no longer pass inimitability on their own.

forces.logic: Big retailers (Foot Locker, Dick's, JD Sports) control shelf space, and consumers switch brands freely; rivals filling the shelves Nike left raise their power. Forces markdowns.
forces.firm_power: Partly: brand still pulls traffic; wholesale rebuilt to $27.5B in FY2026

forces.logic: Many contract factories in Vietnam, Indonesia and China compete for Nike's volume; tariffs (about $1.5B, FY2026) raise costs for the whole industry.
forces.firm_power: Yes: its scale makes it the anchor customer

forces.logic: Adidas, On, Hoka, New Balance and Asics fight on innovation and hype; fashion cycles shift fast; discounting erodes margins.
forces.firm_power: Partly: brand leads overall; lost share in running

forces.logic: Contract manufacturing and social media let brands like On scale fast; global marketing scale still deters most.
forces.firm_power: Yes vs most: scale and athlete deals

forces.logic: Non-sport casual shoes and resale (StockX) substitute only partly; resale often adds hype.
forces.firm_power: Yes: owns the hype resale feeds on

forces.logic: Leagues (NBA, NFL), athletes and social media amplify the brand but charge for access.
forces.firm_power: Yes: long league and athlete contracts

capture.takeaway: Rivalry and retailers cap prices; Nike keeps value only while the brand stays hot.

deliver.statement: Athlete marketing, sport-led innovation, outsourced scale manufacturing and rebuilt wholesale form one brand-heat engine that serves sport-inspired consumers, protects Nike's premium, and wins back retailer shelves; Nike refuses owned factories and low-price lines.

activities.activity: Athlete endorsements and demand creation (Jordan, LeBron)
activities.define_link: Makes Nike the brand of sport for athletes and young sneaker buyers
activities.create_link: Brand heat lifts WTP: the core of the premium
activities.capture_link: Pull demand makes retailers stock Nike despite rivals

activities.define_link: Gives athletes real performance, not just a logo
activities.create_link: Gives the brand something new to sell at full price
activities.capture_link: Differentiation is the only answer to On and Hoka in running

activities.define_link: Keeps product available in every market
activities.create_link: Lowers cost per pair, widening the wedge

activities.capture_link: Repairs retailer (buyer) relationships; wholesale up to $27.5B

deliver.activities_takeaway: Athlete marketing and innovation carry the strategy; the other activities support them.
reinforcement: Athletes → brand heat → full-price sales → margin funds more athletes and innovation → more brand heat
Innovation gives retailers a reason to give Nike shelf space, which puts athletes' stories in front of more buyers
not_do: No owned factories (gives up manufacturing control for flexibility and lower cost)
No low-price segment (leaves value buyers to Skechers and private labels)
misaligned: The 2020-24 direct-to-consumer push cut wholesale partners and ceded shelves to On and Hoka (now reversing)
Leaning on lifestyle franchises (Dunk, Air Force 1) instead of new performance products weakened innovation
judgment: Partly organized: the brand engine is intact, but innovation and channels drifted; Win Now is realigning them (Direct down to $17.7B, wholesale up)
deliver.takeaway: The system depends on one thing: innovation that keeps the brand hot with young consumers.
